pinev: 1896 Atlas of Hamilton Co, Plat of Cass: 'R. S. Bennett 120', a N-S strip in sec 27 W of centre with a house dot, directly N of 'Hamilton County Poor Farm 160' in sec 34, matching the papers ('next to the county poor farm'). BLM PLSS sec 27 = 42.486-42.501, -93.794 to -93.774.

Sept 1898, a month before his death: Reuben Bennett, hermit of 80 owning 300 acres, 'home three miles north of Webster City', hurt in a runaway. Three miles north fits the sec 27 house N of the poor farm; the acreage is given as 300 here and 800 in the obituaries.
N. G. Phillips 44 ac on the river at the 1875 road crossing, N sec 6 Burns Twp (post site per MPHC 1902).

On the USGS 3DEP 10 m DEM the only road crossing of the river in N sec 6 is where roads from the W and E meet the valley near 42.8613,-84.0322; the earlier Cole Rd east-bank gullies pin (42.8615,-84.0295) lies about 220 m E of it, so they are the same crossing and the 300 m ring covers both banks.

1915 Ogle atlas Burns inset: 'Nagg's Bridge, located in E½ Sec 6', where the Grand River Road crosses the Shiawassee; the pin (-84.0322) is in the E½ of sec 6 (BLM PLSS mid-line about -84.0339). Consumers Power Co. held two river parcels at the crossing in 1915; no dam or pond is visible on the 10 m DEM.

1875 atlas: Knaggs Bridge is the Grand River Street bridge over the Shiawassee in sec 6 T5N R4E, hamlet 'Burns P.O.'; a dam just upstream and, on the NE bank above it, a saw mill and grist mill of Roberts & Marshall (about 42.861,-84.031). The Owosso Times, 31 Dec 1897, has Roberts Bros. trading 'their mill property at Knaggs Bridge' for a farm, so the mill hamlet stood through the 1890s. The trading-post tract (N. G. Phillips, 1902) is not labelled on the plat; the gullies S of the bridge remain the target.

Owosso Times 1894: the Williams brothers' trading post stood 'at Knaggs Creek, twelve miles up the river' from Owosso (the Knaggs post's successor site); 1922: an 1851 Indian encampment at Knaggs Bridge, the 2,000-acre reservation sold at $1.25 an acre. No dig story in the Owosso Times 1890-1919.
